title: Association Between Preoperative Locomotive Syndrome Severity and Discharge Disposition After Esophagectomy for Esophageal Cancer: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study
content: Locomotive syndrome reflects mobility impairment arising from dysfunction of the lo-comotive organs, but its clinical relevance to postoperative recovery after esophagec-tomy remains unclear. This single-center retrospective cohort study investigated the association between preoperative locomotive syndrome severity and discharge disposi-tion after esophagectomy for esophageal cancer. Eighty patients who underwent esophagectomy between May 2020 and August 2023 and completed preoperative lo-comotive syndrome assessment were included. Locomotive syndrome was classified into stages 0–3 using the stand-up test, two-step test, and 25-question Geriatric Locomotive Function Scale. Among the 79 patients who survived to hospital discharge, the propor-tion transferred to a rehabilitation hospital increased progressively with locomotive syndrome severity, from 0.0% in stage 0 to 21.2%, 37.5%, and 55.6% in stages 1, 2, and 3, respectively (P = 0.022). Each one-stage increase in locomotive syndrome severity was associated with higher odds of transfer in univariable analysis (odds ratio 2.56, P = 0.005) and remained significantly associated with transfer after adjustment for age and Charlson Comorbidity Index (adjusted odds ratio 2.23, P = 0.031). These findings suggest that preoperative locomotive syndrome severity may help identify patients who are more likely to require transfer to a rehabilitation hospital after esophagectomy.
